problem: Single-shot generative navigation videos often violate physics (35% success), and end-to-end VLA navigation policies entangle intent with control, are huge and slow, and don't transfer easily across embodiments.
motivation: Generative video models are strong at imagining trajectories in pixel space but lack an interface to metric robot control. Separating trajectory imagination from execution could give an embodiment-aware, edge-deployable navigation pipeline.
key_idea: Use an LLM agent loop to generate and validate a first-person reference navigation video (Visual Intermediate Representation), then convert it to velocity commands with a small flow-constrained diffusion transformer (FlowDiT) using DINOv2, optical flow and CLIP conditioning.
insight: The agentic validation loop with memory raises video pass rate from 35% to 86%, and long-term memory cuts iterations from 4.8 to 3.5. Ablation (features zeroed at inference) shows flow improves direction accuracy (67.8 to 76.1) and language enables semantic stopping (SR 65.9 vs 73.4). Open-loop real-robot failures come mainly from video-to-metric scale ambiguity, not from the generated path.
method: Stage I agent loop: an LLM orchestrator routes between WAN 2.2 and LTX-Video, builds prompts with Qwen3-VL, generates 5-15 s videos, and validates with Cosmos-Reason1 (PA, PP, VQ scores; accept if mean >= 80; K_max=5).
Bottleneck-first refinement: a greedy discrete edit of prompts (motion descriptors, camera dynamics, negative prompts, generator switching) targets the lowest-scoring rubric component.
Three-tier memory: static rules.md, long-term memory of successful model/embodiment strategies, and short-term per-task memory of failed attempts.
FlowDiT conditioning: 2304-d vector = DINOv2 goal vision (768) + learned 6-channel CNN optical flow (5.2M params, 256) + live/last-frame DINOv2 obs (768) + CLIP language (512).

FlowDiT policy: DiT with 8 blocks, hidden 512, 8 heads, adaLN-Zero, epsilon-prediction diffusion (T=100), 10-step DDIM, predicts H=8 velocity commands (vx, vy, omega), receding-horizon execution at 40-47 Hz.

Training: pretrain on RECON (11,830 outdoor episodes), fine-tune on 203 Unitree G1 Isaac Sim episodes (162 train/41 val); frozen DINOv2 and CLIP, 43M trainable params; EMA smoothing/velocity clamping post-processing.

setting.backbone: Stage I: LLM orchestrator + Qwen3-VL + WAN 2.2/LTX-Video + Cosmos-Reason1 (frozen); Stage II: FlowDiT (DiT, trained) with frozen DINOv2 and CLIP
setting.training_data: RECON (11,830 outdoor episodes) pretraining + 203 Unitree G1 Isaac Sim episodes fine-tuning
setting.observation: initial RGB image for video generation; generated reference video; optional live RGB (224x224); open-loop uses no live feedback
setting.action_space: continuous velocity commands (vx, vy, omega), horizon 8, normalized [-1,1]

numbers.extra: pretrained RECON + fine-tuned on G1 sim; post-processing; baseline numbers not directly comparable
numbers.evidence: Table ablation: Full FlowDiT 73.4 / 0.293 / 76.1 (Table baselines/abstract report 73.2)

numbers.bench: other:Action Agent Stage I video synthesis (50 tasks)
numbers.evidence: achieves an 86% overall success rate across all embodiments

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only; baseline SRs (ViNT 61, NoMaD 68, OpenVLA 65) are from RECON and not comparable. Per-embodiment Stage I pass: G1 92%, drone 77%, wheeled 83%. Simulation drone/wheeled Stage II SR not reported.
results: Stage I raises video validity from 35% (single-shot) to 86%. FlowDiT gets 73.2% SR on G1 sim val and 64.7% on a real G1 open-loop, with 161x fewer trainable params than OpenVLA, though baseline comparisons are only architectural.
limitations: Baseline comparison is not like-for-like (published RECON numbers vs own G1 sim val); the real-robot evaluation is small (17 trials) and open-loop only
Video-to-metric scale ambiguity and drift; failures in narrow doorframes
Video clips limited to 5-15 s; heavy offline compute for the agentic loop (3.68 s inference for waypoints); Stage II sim results for drone and wheeled robot not reported
